answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table: the release carries a compliance-mandated security patch that must not be reverted. Failover is the wrong tool — the latency correlates with the new release, so the same build would degrade the target region, and shifting write-heavy settlement traffic at peak risks losing customer writes. Adding capacity can't be provisioned fast enough to matter in this window, and a circuit breaker risks failing customer writes, violating the primary objective. Routing read/report queries off the primary is the only low-blast-radius, reversible intervention that doesn't touch the protected release and directly attacks primary contention; memory_b5 records this exact move restoring write latency the same day. Cause is not confirmed (uncertainty preserved — this could still be a release-induced regression), so treat it as a guarded change and keep monitoring write p99; if it doesn't improve, escalate next window.
